report:
Fresh source review of crates.sage_test_harness.compile_tests.rustc_execution using the current start inputs, not the previous verdict. All three ordinary implementation associations and all five annotated test functions were examined. There are no TODO or N/A entries.

Mandatory checking and common inputs: CompileTest has files, edition, observations, diagnostics and queries fields, with no compiler skip option. prepare validates and materializes all files and a minimal dependency-free Cargo manifest, then unconditionally calls rustc::check with that same project, files, edition and markers. The rustc command reads src/lib.rs in that project as crate-type lib. It specifies the selected edition, emits fixture.rmeta with --emit=metadata, and supplies the pinned sysroot; it adds neither --test nor feature cfgs nor a target override. This checks an ordinary library for the compiler host and does not run fixture code. metadata.rs obtains host cfgs from the same compiler. our_sysroot reads the build-time SAGE_SYSROOT and our_rustc derives its bin/rustc path. Captured build.rs obtains and embeds the toolchain sysroot, so the binary and standard library are paired with the host compiler. Metadata-only execution and compiler identity are directly established by the fixed command construction and captured helpers.

Separation and failures: rustc_result is retained while SageHost opens and observe::collect checks the source. Both results are combined only afterward, preserving both source failures. metadata loading returns without compiling the selected crate when direct dependencies are empty, which applies to the generated fixture manifest. The rustc process executes before Sage context capture; prepare clears setup inspection events and observe::collect obtains the Sage check events, so rustc diagnostics checking is separate from dependency metadata and query capture. execute returns a preparation error if spawning fails. validate_output rejects invalid UTF-8 stderr and unexpected stdout, then parses diagnostics and accepts only exit 0 without errors or exit 1 with errors; signals, other exits and inconsistent error/status combinations fail. parse rejects invalid JSON, unexpected record shape/level and malformed fixture spans. quiet_lints also propagates failed compiler startup/inventory errors. Preparation errors cannot reach expectation assertions.

Complete associated test set: (1) pinned_rustc_checks_errors_editions_and_normal_library_configuration asserts an unmarked type error fails, marked type/overflow errors succeed, IntoFuture differs between editions 2024 and 2021, and erroneous test/feature-gated bodies remain disabled. These assertions detect absent rustc checking or accidental test/feature configuration. (2) rustc_is_mandatory_and_warnings_can_be_enabled_in_source asserts quiet ordinary fixtures succeed, an unmarked rustc warning makes prepare fail, a qualified warning succeeds with empty Sage diagnostics, and a qualified deny error succeeds. Thus independent rustc checking is mandatory even when Sage emits no diagnostic. (3) both_compilers_report_source_errors_from_materialized_modules asserts both compiler mismatch messages and the child path for one invalid materialized child module; an early source-error return or omitted child compilation would violate those assertions. (4) malformed_compiler_output_and_invalid_fixture_offsets_fail explicitly rejects non-JSON, empty objects, out-of-range offsets and unsupported diagnostic levels. (5) missing_compiler_and_abnormal_or_inconsistent_output_fail_preparation asserts startup failure on a nonexistent path and validates synthetic outputs for success-with-errors, error-exit-without-errors, unexpected exit 2, signal termination, invalid JSON, invalid UTF-8 and unexpected stdout, plus an accepted empty success control. This last test is Unix-gated because raw signal/status encodings use ExitStatusExt; the remaining associated tests are ordinary cfg(test) tests. Real negative source cases cover the accepted exit 1/error combination. Assertions and fixture setup are visible in the tests; the captured parser/matcher helpers explain their error-count expectations.

Additional dependencies were captured with review read: sage-host/build.rs, annotations.rs parser/compiler selection, and observe.rs collection and matching regions. Current metadata.rs and rustc.rs whole-file inputs contain the remaining execution helpers. No source edits or new behavioral concerns arose in this refresh. This is a source and test-adequacy assessment only: I ran review start/read/record, not behavior tests or a build in this refresh. Root is responsible for centrally running relevant suites under the captured coordinator instructions.
